BiblicalUsage: Zia appears once, in the genealogy of the Gadites who lived in Bashan. He is listed among the heads of their fathers' houses, a man remembered by name even though no story of his is told. The Chronicler keeps his name because every family in Israel counted.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a single-line name still matters to God — Zia is written down because he belonged, and belonging to God's people was never a small thing.
